page.name: Sender identity you own
page.h1: Sender identity stays attached to your accounts
page.metaTitle: Sender identity — numbers and IDs you own
page.metaDescription: The number or ID a message comes from belongs to your account, not to the platform. Registration and verification stay in your name.
page.lede: The sender is the first thing a recipient sees and the thing that decides whether a message is trusted. Because that identity sits on your own account, it stays with you however you choose to send.

sections.h: What a sender identity can be
bullets: Long codes — a standard number, the easiest to obtain and the most heavily rate-limited
Short codes — higher throughput, carrier approval required
Alphanumeric sender IDs — a name instead of a number, supported in some countries only
Toll-free numbers — where the country supports them
p: Which of these you can use depends on the destination country and on your provider. The platform sends from the identity you already hold on the connected account, so it travels with you.

sections.h: Registration is yours, and it is worth doing early
p: Many destinations require the sender to be registered and verified before traffic is accepted — 10DLC and short-code programs being the best-known examples. Those registrations are filed by you, with your provider or the relevant authority, which is also why they sit in your name and stay with you.
bullets: Registration and verification are filed by you, with your provider or the relevant authority
Nothing in the middle can raise a provider quota or lift a carrier filter
An unregistered sender is rejected by the destination network, so registering early is part of going live

p: When a country supports several identity types, throughput and deliverability differ. The practical guidance — when a short code is worth the approval process, and when a second long code is enough — is in the sender selection guide.

faq.a: No. Sender identities belong to the provider account you connect, and the platform sends from the identity already on that account.

faq.q: Will you file a 10DLC registration for us?
faq.a: No — registration and verification are filed by you, in your own name with your provider or the relevant authority.

faq.q: Why does one number send slower than another?
faq.a: Different identity types carry different throughput limits. Long codes are the most limited, which is usually why a second number is added rather than a higher plan bought.
